problem: The step reads "Declare the com.google.android.geo.API_KEY meta-data inside ." — the sentence is cut off and never names the parent XML element. A student following the checklist cannot place the entry, and a misplaced meta-data entry is exactly what produces the grey grid described later.
fix: "Declare a <meta-data> element with android:name=\"com.google.android.geo.API_KEY\" and android:value=\"YOUR_KEY\" inside the <application> element of AndroidManifest.xml."

problem: "In onCreate call getMapAsync(this)" hides two requirements: the fragment must first be obtained with getSupportFragmentManager().findFragmentById(R.id.map), and the activity must implement OnMapReadyCallback for `this` to be a valid argument.
fix: Say: the activity implements OnMapReadyCallback; in onCreate get the fragment by id and call getMapAsync(this) on it.

problem: The text says "the bounding box is the pair of them", which can be read as passing centre and span. newLatLngBounds needs a LatLngBounds built from the corner points, and the chapter never shows how to build it.
fix: Add: build it with new LatLngBounds.Builder().include(new LatLng(lat_min, lon_min)).include(new LatLng(lat_max, lon_max)).build(); the south-west corner is (lat_min, lon_min) and the north-east corner is (lat_max, lon_max).

problem: "Zoom is an integer scale" is not accurate for the Maps SDK. Zoom level is a continuous value (for example 10.5 is legal); only the tile index is the integer floor of it. The useful point is that zoom is not measured in degrees.
fix: Say: zoom is a scale factor (each step doubles the scale), it is not a span in degrees, and it may be fractional; use CameraUpdateFactory.newLatLngBounds to fit a degree span instead of guessing a zoom number.

problem: The reasoning does not explain the error. Both 80.2 and 13.1 are legal values in either slot, so "longitude must stay within −180 to +180" justifies nothing; the point is that the intended point (13.1° N, 80.2° E) becomes a different place near the pole.
fix: "The arguments are swapped: 80.2 is being read as a latitude, so the marker lands near the pole instead of near Chennai. Both numbers are individually legal, which is why no error is raised. Write new LatLng(13.1, 80.2)."

problem: 77.0° N, 12.0° E is in the Norwegian Sea west of Svalbard, not the Arctic Ocean proper.
fix: "puts a Chennai shop in the sea near Svalbard, far inside the Arctic" or simply "near the North Pole".
